bullets.title: US-Iran Military Escalation Threatens Hormuz Shipping; Macro Risk Elevated
bullets.body: US forces conducted three rounds of strikes on Iran within a week, targeting IRGC missile systems, air defenses, and boats near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran declared the strait closed 'until further notice' and launched retaliatory drone/missile strikes on Gulf states including Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, and Jordan—though Trump confirmed the strait remained open to commercial traffic and US/UK maritime authorities affirmed normal transits. Macro commentators noted the strait closure risk as the dominant geopolitical tail risk heading into earnings season, with one macro analyst flagging Hormuz traffic normalization 'not expected before December.'

bullets.title: NVDA Rubin: Supply Chain Nuance—PCB Bottleneck, Not Chip Production
bullets.body: A supply chain analyst noted TSMC chip production for Nvidia's Rubin is on schedule for September, with HBM4 already shipping as of June, but PCB constraints—not chips—represent the real supply risk. Separately, a source citing an 'Expert Call' reported Rubin has been delayed again, though another fintwit user pushed back calling the bear-post trend on NVDA/TSM a deliberate sentiment manipulation play exploiting technical detail amplification. NVIDIA confirmed its roadmap is intact via Morgan Stanley NDR.

bullets.title: SK Hynix CEO: Memory Shortage Persists to 2027 and Beyond; 2027 'Worst Year' for Supply
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO warned 2027 will be the worst year for memory supply in industry history and expects the crunch to persist into the next decade. Despite aggressive capacity expansion, demand will continue to outpace production. The company's record $26.5B US ADR listing opened 14% above its $149 offering price. One analyst noted HBM4E bit exchange rate is 4-5x higher than standard DRAM, a dynamic the market underappreciates.

bullets.title: Micron Commits $250B to US Manufacturing; NY Fab Breaks Ground
bullets.body: Micron announced it expects to invest $250 billion in US manufacturing through 2035 and officially poured concrete for its first New York DRAM megafab in Clay, NY. Analysts noted Wells Fargo raised Western Digital's PT to $730 from $575, and one fintwit account declared MU will likely earn more in 2026 than in the prior 35 years combined.

bullets.title: META Surges 19% in July on AI Chip, Compute Doubling, and Monetization
bullets.body: Meta plans to begin manufacturing its in-house 'Iris' AI chip in September as part of a plan to grow compute from 7GW to 14GW by 2027. The company also started charging businesses to access its AI models for the first time. SemiAnalysis published a positive report on Meta's compute ramp, revealing the company is linking datacenters across 2,000km distances with optical interconnects. META reclaimed its 200-day moving average at the widest margin since January, and Ark Invest purchased 34K shares. Morgan Stanley NDR disclosed Anthropic's compute share on NVIDIA chips has risen to nearly 50%.

bullets.title: TSMC CoWoS Capacity Constrained; Orders Spilling to Intel and Rival Fabs
bullets.body: TSMC cannot keep up with CoWoS advanced packaging demand, forcing orders to Intel and rival Taiwanese fabs. Meanwhile, TSMC is ahead of Samsung in CPO chiplet packaging technology per new PhotonCap field research. Samsung is accelerating its Yongin fab launch to October 2029, two years ahead of schedule. Rapidus set 2nm wafer pricing at ¥3.5M to undercut TSMC.

bullets.title: AI Infrastructure Capex Broadening; Hyperscalers Raise 2026 Guidance Expected
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst argued hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, MSFT, META, ORCL) will raise 2026 full-year capex estimates and 2027 capex indications above consensus. AI infrastructure demand is broadening beyond frontier labs to neocloud providers, European data centers, sovereign compute, and enterprise coding. Big Tech debt doubled to $350B over five years to fund the AI buildout. US ATP imports hit $100B in May, only the second time ever, with Taiwan surpassing China as the third-largest US import source.

bullets.title: AAPL Sues OpenAI for Trade Secret Theft; 400 Apple Employees Recruited
bullets.body: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misappropriation of trade secrets, citing two former Apple engineers (Tang Yew Tan and Chang Liu) who joined OpenAI's hardware team. Apple claims OpenAI's chief hardware officer directed the engineers to bring confidential hardware files, queried suppliers on restricted metal-finishing methods, and asked job candidates to provide proprietary Apple hardware designs. OpenAI has hired approximately 400 people from Apple. The Information reported OpenAI's device launch could come as early as February, but the legal battle poses a major obstacle.

bullets.title: MSFT: GPT-5.6 Integrated into Copilot; 4,800 Layoffs vs. 2,273 H-1B Hires
bullets.body: GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Separately, Microsoft faced backlash after announcing 4,800 layoffs including 1,600 in Xbox while simultaneously being approved to hire 2,273 foreign workers via H-1B. One fintwit account highlighted MSFT expected to grow earnings 64% over three years despite the stock being down 23% YTD, framing the disconnect as a buying opportunity.

bullets.title: Quantum Trade Narrative Shifted in June to Deadline-Focused Procurement
bullets.body: A fintwit analyst noted that June 22 executive orders replaced vague government support with concrete procurement deadlines, transforming the quantum computing trade narrative from sentiment-driven to execution-focused through 2028. Most market participants are still trading on the old thesis, creating a potential mispricing. The QC-ADDS mandate requires delivery of a working quantum computer by 2028.

bullets.title: Semiconductor Stocks See Widest 3% Swing Frequency Since Dot-Com Bubble
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks have moved 3% or more in either direction 15 times in the last 30 trading days, the highest frequency since the Dot-Com Bubble era. Simultaneously, hedge funds bought tech stocks at the fastest pace since October, while the semis sector was the most net-bought subsector of the week but remains heavily net-sold over the past month per hedge fund data.

bullets.title: HOOD Robinhood Chain Momentum: $633M DEX Volume, 70K+ Agentic Trading Accounts
bullets.body: Robinhood's blockchain network hit $633M DEX volume and 306.5K daily active users, with ETH bridged to the chain up ~10x in a week to over $100M. Separately, Robinhood's Agentic Trading feature crossed 70,000 accounts opened since its May launch and is expanding to crypto. CEO Vlad Tenev touted Trump Accounts as a wealth-building vehicle. Analysts called Robinhood Chain the 'most bullish development in the Ethereum ecosystem in years.'

bullets.title: LITE/COHR/AAOI: Photonics Weakness Overdone; Shorts Lack Conviction
bullets.body: Rosenblatt argued photonics sector weakness in AAOI, LITE, and COHR over the past 1-2 months is overdone, with short sellers lacking genuine conviction and expected to cover before earnings beats. LITE was flagged as having already noted InP capacity expansion on recent calls, with InP transitioning from an optics subtopic to a physical AI infrastructure bottleneck. Lumentum's Oleg Shchekin is presenting on VCSEL-based wide-parallel optical interconnects at LightCounting on July 15.

bullets.title: MRVL: Named in Meta and Google Optical Buildouts; 5M Tower PIC Shipments
bullets.body: Marvell landed 5 million tower PIC shipments for AI data center optics. A fintwit analyst also noted Marvell's DSP is being used in Google's coherent-lite infrastructure scale-up and linked it to Meta's inter-datacenter connectivity at 2,000km distances—framing coherent optics as the common infrastructure theme across both hyperscalers' buildouts.

bullets.title: GOOGL: $85B Equity Issuance Seen as Supply Headwind; Interest Expense Up 15x
bullets.body: One analyst argued financial assets peaked on the day Google announced its $85B equity issuance, calling supply drag the primary asset market headwind. Separately, Google's quarterly interest expense exceeded $500M, up 15x year-over-year, driven by AI infrastructure financing. UK financial regulators also formally designated MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, and ORCL as critical third parties subject to direct financial regulatory oversight starting July 13.

bullets.title: China Halts Helium Exports; Global Chip Supply Risk Flagged
bullets.body: China imposed a temporary ban on helium exports amid US-Iran tensions, raising concerns about semiconductor manufacturing supply chains. Helium is critical for chip production. Separately, TSMC 2027 CoWoS capacity is rumored to reach at least 200,000 wafers per month as AI chip packaging demand stays constrained.

bullets.title: AI Frontier Price War Emerging; Token Costs Down 80-90% in Three Years
bullets.body: Fintwit commentary flagged accelerating competition among frontier AI labs, with token cost declining to 10-20% of levels from three years ago. Brad Gerstner argued companies will pay 5x more for best-in-class AI models with no evidence of open-source pricing pressure on quality. Palo Alto's CEO was cited demanding a 90% price drop in AI offerings. Anthropic's ARR was estimated at $69B by Yipit, with daily ARR growth accelerating to ~$550M.

bullets.title: HOOD Robinhood CEO, Trump Accounts, and AI Integration Highlight Earnings Setup
bullets.body: Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev was prominently cited touting Trump Accounts as ownership vehicles building national wealth, as Trump rang the NYSE opening bell for the product launch. HOOD's agentic trading feature and blockchain momentum position it as a key beneficiary of both retail democratization and crypto infrastructure trends heading into earnings.

bullets.title: Investor Sentiment Metrics Flash Caution: Shiller PE Near Dot-Com Peak, Momentum Worst Since COVID
bullets.body: The Shiller PE ratio is approaching its dot-com bubble all-time high. High-Beta Momentum factor saw its worst 5-day performance since COVID. US margin debt as a share of M2 reached 6.2% in May, just below the 6.3% dot-com peak. UBS's proprietary market fragility index hit an all-time high. Investor allocations to cash, bonds, and defensive stocks are near cycle lows. S&P 500 trailing vs. forward P/E gap is near historical extremes.

bullets.title: Fed Report: AI-Induced Memory and Chip Prices Adding 0.5% to Core PCE
bullets.body: The Federal Reserve's semi-annual monetary policy report explicitly cited AI-related factors—including surging memory and chip prices—as driving core PCE inflation higher, with Goldman estimating the combined effect at over 0.2% now rising to 0.5% by year-end. The Fed also flagged hawkish minutes as the most aggressive since 2022, though one analyst argued the rhetoric may be overblown given current inflation swaps. 30-year real yields are pushing back toward multi-decade highs.
